clue.text: Biscuit tin kept by vocalist, heading off during interval

indicators.note: during says the following letters sit inside the word for interval

parts.note: a gap is an interval or space between things

indicators.note: kept by places the tin symbol right after the trimmed vocalist, held at its side
heading off says the word for vocalist loses its first letter

parts.note: a singer is a vocalist
Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

explanation.surface: A singer leaves the stage at half-time, clutching a tin of biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' looks like the singer departing, but it beheads the vocalist; 'kept by' simply sets tin beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ginger snap is a crisp ginger-flavoured cookie, an example of a biscuit.

clue.text: No more work on Tyneside?

parts.note: to go is to work or function, as a machine does
Tyneside, around Newcastle, is in the North East of England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: A lament for vanished jobs in the old shipbuilding region of Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the Newcastle area of north-east England, hence NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no more has departed or ceased to exist; a straight synonym.

clue.text: Painting topless under shade, in retirement, that's spontaneous

indicators.note: under, in a down entry, puts the trimmed painting below the reversed shade
in retirement says the shade word goes backwards, withdrawing

parts.note: tan is a shade of light brown

indicators.note: topless says the painting word loses its first letter

parts.note: a mural is a painting on a wall

explanation.surface: A retired artist painting nude in the shade, quite unselfconsciously.
explanation.walkthrough: TAN reversed 'in retirement' gives NAT; 'topless' cuts MURAL to URAL, set 'under' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural behaviour is unforced and spontaneous; 'that's' turns the definition into an adjectival description.

clue.text: Little energy shown by Ringo, barely playing group's song?

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for energy, the little version of the word

indicators.note: playing says the letters of the next words are performed in a new order

explanation.surface: The Beatles' drummer, scarcely bothering, gives a lacklustre performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' looks like the drummer performing, but it shuffles the two words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A song by the Beatles, the group Ringo Starr drummed for; the question mark marks the definition by example.

clue.text: Right away, tension grips crowd here in London

indicators.note: grips says the shortened tension word holds the crowd word inside
away says the letter for right is removed

parts.note: stress is tension or strain
a jam is a crush or crowd of people

explanation.surface: A crowded London scene with pressure released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' takes R from STRESS, giving STESS; it 'grips' JAM. St James's is a district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: A district of the West End of the capital, near the royal palace, so a place in the city.

clue.text: Bolt maybe retains first place in championships after a flyer

indicators.note: after places the bolt with its insert following the letter A
retains says the bolt word keeps a letter inside it

parts.note: a lock is one kind of bolt, hence maybe

indicators.note: first place in picks the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Usain Bolt keeps his title at the championships, finishing after a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: Usain Bolt the sprinter misleads: the bolt is a LOCK, retaining C. John Alcock flew the first non-stop transatlantic flight in 1919.
explanation.definitionFit: The aviator John Alcock, pilot of the first non-stop Atlantic crossing, is an example of an airman.

clue.text: One calms motorists tense leaving crash

indicators.note: leaving says the tense letter departs from the crash word

parts.note: a thump is a heavy blow or crash
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Tense drivers are soothed after leaving the scene of a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One calms motorists' is a speed hump, which slows (calms) traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed hump is traffic calming: a ridge in the road that forces drivers to slow down.

clue.text: Messy politician tucks into milky dessert (skimmed)

indicators.note: tucks into says the politician is inserted into the dessert word
skimmed says the top letter of the dessert is taken off, like cream off milk

parts.note: junket is a sweet set-milk dessert
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An untidy MP digs into a bowl of low-fat milk pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skimmed' takes J off JUNKET to leave UNKET, into which MP 'tucks'. Junket is a milk set with rennet.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkempt hair or clothes are untidy and dishevelled; a plain synonym.

clue.text: Maths expert terribly hasty to obtain silver and gold — source of profit foremost

indicators.note: foremost says that letter stands at the very front
source of picks the first letter of the following word
to obtain says the jumbled word takes in the metals
terribly signals the word hasty is shuffled

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A greedy mathematician rushes to grab precious metals, profit first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' makes YTHAS; 'to obtain' means to hold the metals inside, and 'foremost' puts the profit letter at the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Pythagoras, the Greek of the right-angled triangle theorem, is the classic mathematician.

clue.text: Chat with seaman providing amphibious thing

parts.note: to natter is to chat idly
a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A gossip with a sailor brings up some creature from the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The natterjack is a European toad, so a land-and-water creature.

clue.text: The latest to park into position for take-off

indicators.note: into says the picked letter goes inside the position word

parts.note: to sit is to be in position

indicators.note: the latest to picks the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Aircraft taxiing into their slots for departure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take-off' looks like an aircraft leaving, but means a parody.
explanation.definitionFit: A take-off is a satirical impersonation, which is what a short comic sketch does.

clue.text: Vehicle Army put in hands of Bill and George, on bends, beneficial

indicators.note: on, in a down entry, places the bends after the rest
put in hands of says the vehicle and army sit between the bill and George letters

parts.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a bill or poster
a van is a vehicle
TA is the Territorial Army
bends shaped like U, so a plural of the letter U, U's

explanation.surface: Bill and George are handed a military vehicle on a winding road.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve. 'bends' is U-bends, so US.
explanation.definitionFit: Something advantageous gives an advantage, so it is helpful or beneficial; a synonym.

clue.text: Press in boxes start to report final for Echo

indicators.note: boxes says the word in surrounds the picked letters
start to picks the first letter of the next word
final for picks the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Reporters pack the start of the story and the closing echo in boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like journalists; it is the verb, to smooth clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To press clothes is to smooth them flat with a hot appliance; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Road surface adverse, cracking nut

parts.note: macadam is a road surface of broken stone

indicators.note: adverse, read as turned against, says the word for cracking runs backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or cracking, written AI

explanation.surface: A rough road surface splits a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' is the adjective meaning excellent: A1, written AI, turned by 'adverse' into IA.
explanation.definitionFit: The macadamia is a round, rich Australian nut, so an example of a nut.

clue.text: Artist led shakily around hospital section, getting attention

indicators.note: around says the shaken letters go round the hospital section
shakily signals the letters of led are jumbled

parts.note: a ward is a section of a hospital
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: An artist, led unsteadily round the ward, wins notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shakily' makes EDL, which goes 'around' the hospital section; 'getting' just joins on the attention word.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear was a Victorian landscape painter and illustrator, as well as the nonsense poet.

clue.text: Lecturer, in entrance unoccupied, outlines Tom's second term in music

indicators.note: in says the lecturer letter goes inside the entrance

parts.note: a door is an entrance

indicators.note: unoccupied empties the next word, keeping only its outer letters
second picks the second letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A lecturer in an empty doorway sketches out the second term's music course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unoccupied' looks like it describes the entrance, but it empties 'outlines' to OS.
explanation.definitionFit: Doloroso is an Italian direction telling players to perform sorrowfully, so a musical marking.

clue.text: Junk food unwrapped on edge of table makes mark on leg?

indicators.note: on places the table letter and food letters after the junk

parts.note: tat is junk or tawdry stuff

indicators.note: edge of picks the outer, first letter of the next word
unwrapped strips the outer letters, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: Junk food dropped from the table leaves a stain on a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwrapped' strips F and D from 'food' to leave OO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is an inked design on the skin, often a leg; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Sample of fiddle, in stereo, found here in Ireland

indicators.note: Sample of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An Irish fiddle tune recorded in stereo.
explanation.definitionFit: Leinster is one of the four provinces of the island, in the east, so a region there.

clue.text: Cunning French king blocks mandate — nothing odd there

indicators.note: blocks says the king sits within the picked letters, obstructing them
nothing odd there keeps only the even letters of the word

parts.note: roi is French for king

explanation.surface: A wily French monarch thwarts an instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing odd there' keeps the even letters of 'mandate', ADT.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and clever, as cunning can mean ingenious; a synonym.

clue.text: Melted brie, smothered in salt, served up as cheesy meal

indicators.note: smothered in says the melted letters lie inside the salt word
served up, in a down entry, says the salt word reads upwards

parts.note: a tar is a sailor or salt

indicators.note: melted says the letters of brie lose their form

explanation.surface: Melted brie, heavily salted, served up for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: TAR reversed by 'served up' is RAT; 'Melted' makes REBI of BRIE, 'smothered in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is cheese melted on toast, so a dish made of cheese.

clue.text: Public ignores old bear, munching bone

indicators.note: ignores says the old letter is left out

parts.note: overt means open or public

indicators.note: munching chews up the letters of bear

explanation.surface: An old bear, unnoticed by the public, gnaws a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignores' removes O from OVERT, leaving VERT; 'munching' makes EBRA of BEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertebra is one of the small bones forming the spine.

clue.text: Without exception, the best farm building?

definitions.meaning: a barn that is number one, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Bar none means with no exceptions; split, it reads as barn one, the top shed.

clue.text: Door requires yellow removing primarily — stripper might do this

indicators.note: requires, read as needs within, says the door holds the picked letters

parts.note: a gate is a door in a wall or fence

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: Instructions for stripping yellow paint off a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripper' looks like a paint remover; it is a striptease dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to revolve or swivel the hips, a move a striptease dancer may perform.

clue.text: Old actress sees Giggs on board relaxing

indicators.note: on, in an across entry, puts the footballer after the jumble
relaxing loosens the letters of board into a new order

parts.note: Ryan Giggs, the Manchester United and Wales footballer

explanation.walkthrough: 'relaxing' makes DORAB of BOARD. Dora Bryan was an English comic actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Dora Bryan was a British stage and film comedienne of the mid twentieth century.

clue.text: Cleaner falls over little black dress

indicators.note: falls over says the cleaner word topples and reads backwards

parts.note: a rag is a cloth for cleaning
B is the abbreviation for black, as in pencil grades

explanation.surface: A cleaner trips over a little black dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little black dress' looks like one phrase; 'dress' is the definition alone. RAG reversed by 'falls over' is GAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing or attire, so dress in its general sense.

clue.text: Ring Oriental in China

indicators.note: in says the oriental letter goes inside the friend word

E is short for east, the orient

explanation.walkthrough: China means pal from British rhyming slang (china plate = mate).
explanation.definitionFit: A peal is a ringing of bells, so ring as a noun or verb of bells.

clue.text: European runner emitting pained cry, joint last in race

indicators.note: emitting says the cry is let out of the joint word

parts.note: the elbow is an arm joint
ow is a cry of pain

indicators.note: last in picks the final letter of the next word

explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' looks like an athlete; it is a river. 'emitting' takes OW from ELBOW, leaving ELB.

clue.text: By 7 in morning, one's gazing at Galaxy endlessly?

definitions.text: By 7 in morning, one's gazing at Galaxy endlessly?

parts.note: a stargazer studying the galaxy is an astronomer

clue.text: List of names, Aaron-Rupert, initially rejected?

indicators.note: rejected, read as thrown back, says the phrase runs backwards

parts.note: the initials A and R, with the dash read as to, give A to R

explanation.walkthrough: The initials with the dash read 'A to R', like an index; reversed, R to A.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a schedule of people taking turns, a list of names.

clue.text: Film-maker understanding sport's market

parts.note: ken is knowledge or understanding

to market is to sell

explanation.surface: A film-maker who understands the sports market.
